exec_signals.text: Brent up 3.8% today on Hormuz partial closure threat
Net reserves down to 15.2bn USD, 4-month import cover
DSEX breadth 0.52 adv/dec for fifth straight negative session
BB holds 10.00% rate; real rate still negative at CPI 9.1%
10yr yield at 11.85%; bank duration books under pressure
IMF tranche review postponed; timeline unclear
Remittance Apr MTD 1.82bn USD, up 6.5% yoy ahead of pace

iranwar.meaning: Iran signalling Strait controls has pushed Brent to 88.4 USD/bbl, a 3.8% single-day spike that feeds directly into Bangladesh fuel subsidy cost and LC opening pressures.
iranwar.action: Cap new commodity LCs at 90-day sight for any Hormuz-route crude cargo until risk premium settles below 3 USD/bbl.
iranwar.trigger: Watch Brent above 92 USD/bbl as the threshold where BB may issue a forex conservation circular.
iranwar.focus: Energy-sector borrowers with floating fuel cost exposure need a stress test at 95 USD/bbl scenario this week.
iranwar.pull: Oil shock + Hormuz premium = LC cost escalation imminent.

fx.meaning: Net reserves at 15.2bn USD represent barely four months of import cover, the lowest since the 2022 crisis, with further drawdown likely if oil import bills rise.
fx.action: Prioritise export-backed FCY deposit mobilisation; avoid approving new FCY loans against BDT collateral until reserves stabilise above 16bn USD.
fx.trigger: A weekly reserves print below 15.0bn USD net would signal BB intervention and likely trigger crawling-peg ceiling breach.
fx.focus: Clients with bullet USD repayments in May-June are at elevated rollover risk given current BDT softness.
fx.pull: Reserve drawdown trend is the single biggest macro risk on the desk this week.

bb.meaning: BB holding at 10.00% for a third consecutive meeting confirms the MPC believes inflation momentum is contained, but real rates remain negative at minus 0.9% against CPI of 9.1%.
bb.action: Lock in 3-year fixed-rate SME loans at current SMART-linked floors before any eventual rate normalisation erodes spread.
bb.trigger: A CPI print above 9.5% for two consecutive months would likely force BB to resume hiking, repricing the entire loan book.
bb.focus: NBFI liability pricing still lags the policy rate; review term deposit re-pricing schedules for Q2.
bb.pull: Rate hold is dovish signal — but negative real rates keep inflation risk alive.

macro.meaning: CPI at 9.1% with a 0.2pp monthly uptick on food prices confirms that last mile disinflation is stalling, undermining the case for an early rate cut.
macro.action: Build CPI sensitivity into credit models; sectors exposed to food retail and agri supply chains warrant a 50bp risk premium add.
macro.trigger: A GDP growth revision below 5.0% official estimate would compress tax revenue and widen fiscal space needed for IMF programme targets.
macro.focus: Core CPI at 7.8% suggests non-food demand pressures remain; watch wage-driven services inflation in Q2.
macro.pull: Sticky CPI + slowing GDP = stagflation risk creeping into the base case.

tbond.meaning: The 10yr yield edging to 11.85% reflects market scepticism about the pace of fiscal consolidation and elevated supply from the government auction calendar.
tbond.action: Trim HTM bond portfolio duration below 5 years; favour floating-rate tbill ladder over long-dated fixed-coupon paper at current spreads.
tbond.trigger: A 10yr auction devolvement or cut-off above 12.25% would signal primary dealer demand destruction and warrant immediate ALM review.
tbond.focus: Banks carrying large AFS bond books face mark-to-market losses if yields breach 12.00%; model the P&L impact now.
tbond.pull: Duration risk is underpriced — act before yields test 12%.

dse.text: DSEX at 5218 on thin 382cr turnover signals institutional absence; five-day negative breadth (adv/dec 0.52) reflects broad risk-off positioning. Equities are not the priority read today — Hormuz and reserves dominate.
